SMTO-HTTP-0071 — The request said one kind of content but carried another

GUID: 61caa331-df59-49c2-a180-7495d5e1deab
Slug: http-content-type-conflict
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO was about to send data to a web service, but the label describing that data didn't match what was inside. It stopped before sending anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to resend the request and let it choose the content type for the data automatically. SMTO sets the right content label on its own when one isn't forced, so the label and the data match.
  2. If the request uses a saved connection, open Parameter Store, select that connection, and look under Advanced connection settings for a Default header named Content-Type. Remove it and save. A default content label is added to every request on that connection, even ones that send a different kind of data.
  3. If the service only accepts one kind of data (for example a form), tell SMTO which kind in the conversation. SMTO can then build the data in the format the service expects instead of guessing.

What success looks like

  • The request is sent and the step shows the service's reply instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's connections. Nothing was sent, so you don't need to check the service for changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • prepare_request rejected the request because its Content-Type contradicts the selected body mode, declares a non-UTF-8 charset, or sets a multipart Content-Type the runtime must generate.

What this means

  • Content-Type disagrees with the selected body mode, declares a non-UTF-8 charset, or manually supplies a multipart boundary owned by the encoder. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Content-Type disagrees with the selected body mode, declares a non-UTF-8 charset, or manually supplies a multipart boundary owned by the encoder.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare mode, media type and charset; let the multipart encoder provide its own boundary.

How to fix it

  • Make the Content-Type header agree with the body mode: application/json for json_body, application/x-www-form-urlencoded for form_body, and charset=utf-8 (or none) for text. For multipart_body, remove the manual Content-Type so the Gateway adds its own boundary; also check default_headers in the saved HTTP profile.
  • Use the body mode that matches the endpoint. Remove manual multipart Content-Type so the runtime supplies the boundary; align text charset with UTF-8.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The final Content-Type accurately describes the supported encoded body.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
